# Markdown

Markdown is a way to make fancy documents.
Make sure you "knit" often -- after every major change -- to mitigate errors.
Hastags are how we make section levels of a doc.

# Basic formating

This is **bold** (that's doble astrisks). Or *italics*. or `code`

- this is the start of a list.
- next item.
- nest item. Make sure you have a space at the end of the item. 

1. this is a numbered list.
2. second item. 

* this is a bulleted list 
* next item

To add a hyperling, do `[link test](url)`without backticks. For example [go here](https://new.sewanee.edu/)

To link to sections of your document, do `[link text](#section-name)`, without backtics, with hyphens for spacees, and everything lowercase. for example, [go here](#markdown).

To add mor vertical space between blocks of text, use "nbsp;" withought quates.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Should be more space now.

**To include an image -- fun!**
first pput an image inside the folder where your `Rmd` file is located. Then type `![](full_immage-filename-here){width = "50%"}`

# RMarkdown

`RMarkdown` is just `Markdwon` with`R` code woven in.

You can do R stuff in the same line as text `r 3+3` will show as 6.

you can also do a full-multi-line CHUNK of R stuff:
```{r chunk-name} 
#```{r}
3 + 3
#```
```

setting to control how R chunks appear:

- `eval = TRUE` : which actually runs the code; if `FALSE`, it shows the code but doesn't run it. 
- `echo = TRUE` : which shows the code; if `FALSE`, the code can run withought beeing seen. 
- `warnings = FALSE` : which will turn off warnings. 
- `fig.cap = "figure caption"` adds a figure caption. 
- `fig.height = 4` example of figure height 
- `fig.width = 7` example of figure width


```{r, eval = TRUE}
#this will be shown
3 + 3
```

```{r, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
# this will be evaluated but not shown
4 + 4
```

# Bringing in real data

To manually set working directiry while building up my RMarkdown file, just to to Session > Sew working directory > Source file location
```{r read data, }
library(readr)
energy <- read_csv("../data/IRENA data.csv", skip = 1)

```
```{r espore data, }
library(dplyr)
energy %>% names
energy %>% head
energy %>% tail
energy %>% pull(Technology) %>% unique %>% sort
energy %>% pull(`Country/area`) %>% unique

```
### Filtering code now
```{r}
# filter data
fenergy <- energy %>%
  filter(`Country/area` == 'United States of America (the)')

```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
p <- ggplot(fenergy,
       aes( x = Year,
            y = as.numeric(`Electricity statistics`),
            fill = Technology
            )) +
  geom_area()

ggplotly(p)
```
